# [USBD05] Physical Instantiation and Data Population in Oracle SQL

* **Priority:** High
* **Story Points:** 5
* **Module / Component:** `BDDAD` / `Database`
* **Status:** In Progress

---

## 👤 User Story Description

**As a** Product Owner
**I want** the relational model to be instantiated in an Oracle SGBD using the SQL DDL code generated by an appropriate tool
**So that** the ShopRobot applications (Shopping, Planning and Administration) share one database whose data integrity can be verified

## 💬 Customer Specifications & Clarifications

* **Specification (Project Specification v1, 7.3.1):** the DDL must be generated by an appropriate tool; USBD04 allows the physical script to be generated "by a specific tool or an LLM".
* **Specification (Section 4.1):** a retailer may own several shopping locations; a shopping location has several levels served by elevators; each level has areas (amenity, indoor, shop, highway).
* **Specification (Section 4.2):** usually one robot station per level, except customer parking levels; each station has one control terminal; robots in use are not parked.
* **Specification (USEI04):** assigning a robot changes it from `READY` to `BUSY` and frees a spot in its station.
* **Specification (USEI05):** the sub-orders of one order are assigned to distinct robots; refrigerated items go in refrigerated robots.
* **Out of Scope:** the PL/SQL API (NFR02) and triggers that enforce the rules of [Part C](#rules-checked-by-query) (future sprints).

## 🔒 Non-Functional Requirements & Security

* **NFR01 - Business Rules:** rules are enforced by `PRIMARY KEY`, `UNIQUE`, `FOREIGN KEY`, `CHECK`, `NOT NULL` and function-based unique indexes; rules that need several rows are checked by query (Part C) until the PL/SQL API exists.
* **NFR02 - Database:** single Oracle schema shared by all applications.
* **NFR05 - Documentation / Naming:** tables in `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`, constraints prefixed `pk_`, `uk_`, `fk_`, `ck_`, `nn_`, indexes `ux_`.
* **Generative AI (Section 3.6):** the DDL, the test data and the queries were drafted with Claude (Anthropic) from the domain model and reviewed by the team.

### Domain model → tables

| Domain class / association | Table | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `SystemUser` + `UserRole` | `APP_USER` | `user_role` with `CHECK`; `UNIQUE (user_id, user_role)` used by role FKs |
| `RetailerCompany` | `RETAILER_COMPANY` | PK `vat_number` |
| `ShoppingLocation` | `SHOPPING_LOCATION` | FK to retailer; `geo_json_data` is a `CLOB` with `CHECK IS JSON` |
| `Level` | `SHOPPING_LEVEL` | `LEVEL` is reserved in Oracle; PK `(location_id, level_number)` |
| `Area` (abstract) | `AREA` | discriminator `area_type`; `polygon_coordinates` is JSON |
| `Shop`, `RobotStation`, `Amenity`, `DeliverySpot`, `Corridor` | `SHOP`, `ROBOT_STATION`, `AMENITY`, `DELIVERY_SPOT`, `CORRIDOR` | one table per subclass, PK = FK `(area_id, area_type)` to `AREA` |
| `Elevator` | `ELEVATOR` | |
| `Level` 2..* — 1..* `Elevator` | `ELEVATOR_LEVEL` | association table |
| `ControlTerminal` | `CONTROL_TERMINAL` | `UNIQUE (station_area_id)` → 1:1 with station; operator must be `MAINTENANCE_OPERATOR` |
| `Robot` + `RobotStatus` | `ROBOT` | operates in one shopping location; station is optional (0..1) |
| `StationMovement` | `STATION_MOVEMENT` | scheduled entry/exit of a robot in a station |
| `Product` | `PRODUCT` | FK to shop |
| `ShoppingCart`, `CartItem` | `SHOPPING_CART`, `CART_ITEM` | at most one cart per customer |
| `Order` + `OrderStatus` | `CUSTOMER_ORDER` | `ORDER` is reserved; customer must be `CUSTOMER`; FK to delivery spot |
| `SubOrder` + `SubOrderStatus` | `SUB_ORDER` | robot is optional (0..1) |
| `OrderItem` | `ORDER_ITEM` | PK `(order_id, product_id)`; FKs to product and sub-order+order; the shop is the product's shop |
| `Route`, `Stop` | `ROUTE`, `STOP` | route planned by a `SYSTEM_PLANNER` for one sub-order |

### Main design decisions

* **Disjoint `Area` hierarchy:** each subtype has `area_type` fixed by a `CHECK` and a composite FK `(area_id, area_type)` to `AREA`, so an area cannot be a shop and an amenity at the same time.
* **User roles in associations:** `SHOP.merchant_role`, `CUSTOMER_ORDER.customer_role`, `SHOPPING_CART.customer_role`, `CONTROL_TERMINAL.operator_role` and `ROUTE.planner_role` are fixed by `CHECK` and part of the FK to `APP_USER (user_id, user_role)`, so e.g. only a merchant can manage a shop and only a customer can place an order.
* **3NF of `ORDER_ITEM`:** the shop of an item is not stored (it is the shop of its product); FK `(sub_order_id, order_id)` to `SUB_ORDER` guarantees the sub-order belongs to the same order.
* **GeoJSON import (USLP06):** `SHOP.shop_code` and `SHOP.merchant_id` are optional, so imported shops can be inserted.
* **Robot state vs. station:** `READY`/`CHARGING` robots are in a station, `BUSY` robots are not, `MAINTENANCE` robots can be either.
* **Robot assignment:** unique index `ux_sub_order_order_robot` → sub-orders of one order use distinct robots (USEI05); unique index `ux_sub_order_active_robot` → a robot has at most one active sub-order *(to confirm)*; `ck_sub_order_robot` → only `PENDING` sub-orders may have no robot.
* **Composition** (filled diamond) → `ON DELETE CASCADE`; aggregation (`SubOrder o-- OrderItem`) → no cascade.
* **Booleans** → `CHAR(1)` `'Y'`/`'N'`; **enumerations** → `VARCHAR2` + `CHECK IN`.
* **IDs** are fixed and deterministic (BDDAD clarification of 2026-10-09).

### Rules checked by query

These rules involve several rows or tables and cannot be written as a declarative constraint in Oracle. They are checked by Part C of [03_verification_queries.sql](../../DataBase/scripts/03_verification_queries.sql) (each query must return no rows) and will be enforced by the PL/SQL API / triggers:

| Rule | Query |
| :--- | :--- |
| Robots in a station ≤ station capacity | C1 |
| An elevator connects ≥ 2 levels of one shopping location | C2 |
| Every level has ≥ 1 elevator | C3 |
| Every retailer has ≥ 1 shopping location; every shopping location has ≥ 1 level | C4 |
| Every area belongs to its subtype table (abstract `Area`) | C5 |
| Every robot station has a control terminal | C6 |
| Every order has ≥ 1 item and ≥ 1 sub-order; every sub-order has ≥ 1 item | C7 |
| Load of a sub-order ≤ weight/volume capacity of its robot | C8 |
| Refrigerated products only in refrigerated robots | C9 |
| Shops of an order are in the location of its delivery spot | C10 |
| Robot with an active sub-order is `BUSY` and vice-versa | C11 |
| A `DELIVERED` order has all its sub-orders `DELIVERED` | C12 |
| Refrigerated and normal products never in the same sub-order (client, 2026-10-12) | C13 |
| Every product can be carried by a robot of its location (client, 2026-10-02) | C14 |
| A robot's station, orders and movements are in the robot's location | C15 |
| A route has ≥ 2 stops, pickups at shops, last stop = delivery at the order's spot | C16 |

### Test data scenarios

| Scenario in the data | Shows |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Norte Retail Group` owns NorteShopping and Shopping Douro | a retailer owns several locations |
| NorteShopping has levels −1, 0 and 1; level −1 is parking with no robot station | Section 4.2 (stations per level) |
| Elevator `EL-NS-01` serves 3 levels, `EL-NS-02` serves 2 | M:N level–elevator |
| Shops, amenities, robot stations, delivery spots and corridors (`NS-A016`, `SD-A013`) | every `Area` subtype |
| Merchant `U010` manages three shops; shop `NS-A021` is closed; shop `NS-A026` was just imported from the GeoJSON (no merchant, no code) | merchant–shop (0..1), `is_open`, USLP06 |
| Users of all six roles; customer `U004` has no orders but has a cart; retailer admin `U020` works for Norte Retail Group | `UserRole`, 0..* orders, shopping cart |
| Station `ST-NS-0` is full (3/3), `ST-NS-1` has 1 free spot | USEI02 |
| Robots in all four states; `BUSY` robots out of the stations; `R013` in maintenance outside a station | `RobotStatus`, 0..1 station |
| Orders in all five states and sub-orders in all five states | `OrderStatus`, `SubOrderStatus` |
| `O0002` has items from 3 shops, split into a refrigerated sub-order (robot `R007`) and a normal one (`R008`); `O0004`, `O0007` and `O0008` are also split to keep refrigerated items apart | USEI05, client 2026-10-12 |
| Pending `O0003` can be carried by `R001`/`R005`; pending `O0008` has refrigerated items and no refrigerated robot is `READY` | USEI04 (feasible / not feasible) |
| Every product fits in at least one robot of its location (e.g. `P016`, 40 kg / 110 L, fits `R012`) | client 2026-10-02 |
| Routes `RT0001`/`RT0002` of the sub-orders of `O0002`, with pickups and delivery | route planning |
| Station movements: past exits/entries and a scheduled entry (`MV0005`) | schedule of robot movements |

## Edge Cases

* **Re-running the scripts:** `00_drop_tables.sql` drops only the ShopRobot tables and ignores the ones that do not exist.
* **Location without GeoJSON yet:** `geo_json_data` is optional (`LOC-OA`), because it is filled by the import of USLP06.
* **Deleting a station with parked `READY` robots:** rejected, because `ON DELETE SET NULL` would leave a `READY` robot outside a station (`ck_robot_status_station`).

## 🧪 Functional Tests / Validation

How to run on Oracle FreeSQL:

1. Sign in at [freesql.com](https://freesql.com) and open a worksheet.
2. Run, in this order, as a script: `00_drop_tables.sql`, `01_create_tables.sql`, `02_insert_data.sql`.
3. Run `03_verification_queries.sql` and check the results below.
4. Run `04_constraint_tests.sql` and check the DBMS output.

| Scenario ID | Test Case / Steps | Expected Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TC-01** | Run `00`, `01` and `02` | No errors; 23 tables created; `COMMIT` complete |
| **TC-02** | Part A of `03` | 23 rows, every `num_rows` > 0 |
| **TC-03** | B3 (USLP04) | Levels −1, 0, 1 of NorteShopping; level 0 stores: Desporto Total, Mercearia do Norte, Moda Viva |
| **TC-04** | B6 / B7 (USEI02) | `ST-NS-0` capacity 3, occupied 3, free 0; robots R001 (95), R003 (70), R002 (40) |
| **TC-05** | B9 (USEI03) | Pending orders: `O0008` (12:15) before `O0003` (13:00) |
| **TC-06** | B12 (USEI04) | `O0003` feasible with R001 (95) then R005 (76); `O0008` NOT FEASIBLE |
| **TC-07** | B13 (USEI05) | `O0002` split in `SO0002` (R007, refrigerated) and `SO0003` (R008); also `O0004`, `O0007`, `O0008`; loads within capacity |
| **TC-08** | Part C (C1-C16) of `03` | Every query returns no rows |
| **TC-09** | Run `04` | `Passed: 47   Failed: 0`; data unchanged afterwards |

## ❓ Assumptions to confirm with the client

* An `Area` is always one of the four subtypes (the domain model marks it abstract); corridors and elevators of the GeoJSON are not stored as areas yet.
* The minimum battery to assign a robot is 20 % (used only in query B12).
* An order item stays in a single sub-order (quantity of a product is not split between robots), as in the domain model.
* A `MAINTENANCE` robot can be outside a station.
* Control terminal IPs are IPv4.
